posts.text: If your wallet is small and it’s still not growing, read this. You don’t need bigger trades. You need better risk management. Let’s say you have a $200 wallet. Before entering any trade, decide one thing first: “How much am I okay losing if this trade is wrong?” For example, fix your maximum risk at $5 per trade. Now don’t randomly put $5 as margin and choose 20x leverage. That’s not how it works. First find your entry, then find the technical stop-loss the level where your trade idea becomes invalid. Suppose your SL is 5% away. Maximum risk = $5 SL distance = 5% Position size = $5 ÷ 5% = $100 Only after this calculate the leverage according to the margin you want to use. If you use $10 margin: $100 ÷ $10 = 10x leverage So if the 5% SL gets hit, your planned loss is around $5, not your whole account. According to Odaily, the case involved a victim who exchanged $50,000 for Bitcoin and transferred it to a criminal group; the court said the Bitcoin was not valueless intangible data but property that could be the subject of a property crime. posts.text: The U.S. Treasury sold $70 billion in five-year notes at a yield of 4.845%, above the 4.841% when-issued level at the 1 p.m. New York bidding deadline. According to Sina Finance, the higher yield indicated demand was slightly weaker than expected. Although performance improved significantly from the previous month, this was the 12th consecutive weak auction for this maturity. The five-year yield was up about 1 basis point on the day before the results and rose about 1.5 basis points after their release, flattening the 5s30s yield curve further. Primary dealers received 10.6% of the notes, below the previous auction; indirect bidders' share recovered to 60%, while direct bidders' share fell to 29.4%. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.33, above the 2.31 average for the previous six auctions.

It is the CFTC’s tenth lawsuit against a state, following cases involving Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, New York, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Rhode Island, New Mexico and Kentucky. Separately, Reuters reported on Tuesday that the CFTC is investigating Polymarket over whether it violated a 2022 agreement to bar U.S. users from its flagship overseas platform.

U.S. consumer confidence unexpectedly rose in October for the first time in four months as views of the job market and business conditions improved. Brent crude fell 1.8% to around $114 a barrel. Iran's leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, reaffirmed conditions for ending the war with the United States during a meeting with the country's security chief. Amid intensified regional diplomacy, some Gulf Arab states called for a coordinated security agreement to end the conflict. posts.text: According to CNBC, annual growth in margin debt fell to 31.4% in September from 53.7% in May, based on FINRA data cited by Bank of America technical strategist Paul Ciana. Ciana said slowing borrowing momentum after extreme levels has coincided with previous market peaks. May’s growth rate in 2026 was the fourth highest since 1998; the three higher readings occurred in 2000, 2007 and 2021, each before a stock market decline. Margin debt totaled $1.48 trillion in September, 1.5% below June’s record of $1.5 trillion. Bank of America also cited widening high-yield credit spreads and a rotation toward defensive sectors, which its equity derivatives team said had reached bubble-risk levels.

posts.text: Meta is boosting its equity offering to almost $98 billion, one of the largest ever, as it increases its AI investment, according to Bloomberg. Anthropic’s potential IPO could be a defining test for the AI boom; its S-1 filing shows growth, spending and losses. Anduril is teaming up with chipmaker Qualcomm to build a laptop with a U.S. supply chain, founder Palmer Luckey said.

posts.text: According to CNBC, Amazon’s memo on AI use by software engineers discourages “tokenmaxxing” and says employees should use AI tools selectively. Circulated internally in September and posted to Amazon’s website on Tuesday, the memo revises how the company defines software engineers’ and managers’ roles in the age of AI. Amazon said token usage, AI-tool adoption rates and code changes or reviews are flawed measures of teams’ AI use and should be assessed carefully alongside other data. The company said employees should focus on long-term outcomes and that not using AI for a task can be an appropriate judgment. An Amazon spokesperson said the company has not capped employees’ token use. In May, Amazon shut down an internal leaderboard after finding employees were using tokens to climb the rankings.

Familiarity with digital assets was lower: 9% of respondents said they were familiar with crypto, and 5% with stablecoins. posts.text: Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Luiz Fux will hold a public hearing on November 3 concerning the ban on sports betting and online casinos. According to Odaily, Fux has not ruled on whether to suspend the ban; the hearing is scheduled for 10 a.m. local time and will focus on the ban’s economic effects. The ban took effect on October 25, rendering 85 Brazilian gambling licenses invalid. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won re-election that same day, and industry group ANJL called for renewed dialogue with the government. The hearing will include 26 participants, among them parties to related lawsuits, government agencies, football clubs and industry groups. Individual gambling operators were not invited. Congress was initially required to vote on the provisional measure by November 23; the deadline may be extended once, for up to 60 days.

Johnson also said Republicans would keep their House majority. The remarks came during a campaign stop with New York Republican Rep. Mike Lawler, one week before the Nov. 3 midterm election.

Royal Caribbean said third-quarter guest numbers rose 9% year over year to 2.7 million and 2027 bookings were up in the high teens. Sherwin-Williams reported a 7.9% increase in net sales, while UPS said U.S. revenue rose 4.5% to $14.86 billion and raised its full-year revenue forecast to approximately $92.6 billion from $91.2 billion. posts.text: According to Jin10, Stephen Jones of Aegon’s asset management division said Wednesday’s UK budget is unlikely to bring surprises because the government lacks both fiscal room and the political will for bold measures. However, he said even a modest surprise could unsettle markets before Halloween when investors are prepared for a subdued budget. UK government bond prices have continued to rise in recent weeks as market sentiment toward UK assets has turned more positive. Jones said the tail risk from additional borrowing lies not in the budget speech itself but in the deeper mechanics of fiscal operations. He said markets could absorb about £10 billion in additional financing, perhaps raised through off-balance-sheet instruments, but a further £30 billion to £40 billion increase in gilt issuance would be harder for them to accept.

posts.text: According to Jin10, Standard Chartered strategists said in a report that over the past 30 years, the most favorable market environment for risk-sensitive currencies has been one in which U.S. stocks rise alongside Treasury yields. Early in an economic recovery, yields are often low, reflecting accommodative monetary policy and insufficient credit demand. As optimism about the growth outlook increases, the shift is typically reflected in stocks, bond yields, and currencies positively correlated with risk sentiment, including the Canadian dollar, Australian dollar, Norwegian krone, Mexican peso, and New Zealand dollar. The strategists said the relationship may be less reliable if rising yields reflect a higher risk premium or increased inflation risks.

posts.text: According to Jin10, KPMG Canada Chief Economist Ali Jaffery said he was not inclined to support a Bank of Canada rate hike on Wednesday but did not consider such a move a policy mistake. Despite job losses and weakening market sentiment in Canada, the central bank appears determined to address inflation risks from persistently high oil prices preemptively. If it raises rates by 25 basis points and then hikes again, the policy rate would remain within the central bank’s estimated neutral-rate range. The neutral rate is a level that neither restrains nor stimulates economic activity. Jaffery said a rate hike could prolong Canada’s weak economic period, but added that central bank officials may believe the economy still has enough favorable factors to support continued growth.

posts.text: According to Jin10, major Gulf stock markets rose early Tuesday after senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran the previous day in an effort to ease the escalating military conflict. It was the first high-level contact between Iran and the three countries since they signed a mutual defense agreement in August this year. The war, which began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran, has spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen. Saudi Arabia’s benchmark index rose 0.5%, Dubai’s main index gained 0.6%, Qatar’s index advanced 1% and Abu Dhabi’s index climbed 0.3%, with bank stocks leading gains in most markets. DIP Holding, which owns a real estate project in Dubai Investment Park, is seeking to raise up to $543 million through an IPO. If successful, it would be the UAE’s first potential IPO this year.

Gulf members' oil exports were interrupted for several months amid Iran-related conflict, and those countries are now working to increase exports; however, actual output for most members remains well below their targets. The sources said no final decision has been made.

posts.text: CoreWeave (NASDAQ: $CRWV) Stock Falls 4.17% as HSBC Maintains $39 Target Amid Debt Concerns. CoreWeave shares fell 4.17% to $58.57 in Tuesday’s premarket trading after HSBC maintained its Reduce rating and $39 price target, implying 36.5% downside from Friday’s $61.39 close. The bank warned that rising borrowing costs and weaker AI computing demand could pressure profitability. The stock had already dropped 25.2% last week, while Monday’s trading volume reached about 101 million shares, more than three times its three-month average. HSBC estimates CoreWeave’s 2027 annual revenue per megawatt at $12 million, below the $17 million–$18 million projected for larger cloud providers. However, Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to Buy, arguing that investors may be overstating financing risks and underestimating future returns. posts.text: Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ: $CBRS) Stock Falls 3.46% as TD Cowen Cuts Price Target by $100. Cerebras shares fell 3.46% to $116.48 in Tuesday’s premarket trading after TD Cowen cut its 12-month price target from $275 to $175 while maintaining a Buy rating. The stock lost about 15.1% over two sessions and traded below its $185 IPO price. Despite the reduction, TD Cowen’s revised target remains roughly 50% above the premarket price. The cut comes amid questions about Cerebras’ role in powering OpenAI’s latest high-speed AI service. SemiAnalysis reported that GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast runs on Nvidia GPUs, but neither company has confirmed the hardware supplier. OpenAI has committed to purchasing 750 megawatts of Cerebras computing capacity through 2028, while Cerebras reported $25.4 billion in remaining performance obligations as of June 30. #CryptoNewss

posts.text: New XRP Wallet Receives 82.3 Million Tokens Worth $106 Million in Single Transfer. A newly activated XRP wallet received 82,314,668 XRP worth more than $106 million on October 20. Nearly 12 hours later, it still held the entire amount, with no recorded outflows. The sending address retained approximately 142.7 million XRP worth $184 million after the transfer. The sending address has repeatedly received XRP from another wallet linked to Binance, with large transfers between the addresses dating back to November 2025. However, the identity of the wallet owners remains unknown. The latest transfer could involve a large investor moving funds or Binance shifting assets between wallets, but the available records do not confirm either explanation. #Crypto

posts.text: Pro-XRP lawyer Bill Morgan has argued that the SEC lawsuit can no longer serve as an excuse for XRP’s disappointing price performance. In an X post, he noted that the coin has continued to decline despite the legal dispute’s resolution. Specifically, Morgan said XRP had fallen 45% over the past 12 months and approximately 60% since the litigation with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) was resolved on August 7, 2025. “The lawsuit cannot be an excuse all the time for XRP’s current price. That excuse is getting quite old,” Morgan wrote. He described the legal dispute as an “overrated and exaggerated excuse,” arguing that positive developments in the case often lifted XRP’s price temporarily, but those gains were largely reversed afterward. posts.text: Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: $INTC) Stock Rises 4.16% Pre-Market After JPMorgan Upgrades Rating to Neutral. JPMorgan upgraded Intel from Underweight to Neutral, ending a negative rating it had maintained since November 2022. The upgrade sent Intel shares climbing 4.16% to $93.59 in pre-market trading Monday. Analyst Harlan Sur said the stock’s 36% decline from its June peak had reduced potential downside, while improving execution under CEO Lip-Bu Tan had increased his confidence in the company’s turnaround. Despite the upgrade, JPMorgan kept its $85 price target, below the current share price. The bank pointed to progress in chip manufacturing, production yields, advanced packaging, and demand for CPUs used in AI systems.
